scope: Source-checked regulatory labeling annotations; no molecular binding label, individual efficacy estimate or clinical recommendation

annotations.regulatory_summary: FDA permits conditional risk-reduction wording under enforcement discretion; this is not an authorized claim meeting significant scientific agreement.
use_conditions: At least 84 mg elemental magnesium per reference amount customarily consumed (RACC).
Dietary supplements must supply no more than 350 mg/day magnesium when used as labeled.
Conventional foods must meet the low-sodium criterion; general health-claim rules and other letter factors apply.
Qualifying language must communicate the weak and conflicting evidence.

disease_scope: coronary heart disease through blood-pressure reduction
annotations.regulatory_summary: Combined EPA+DHA risk-reduction wording is conditional and below the significant-scientific-agreement threshold.
use_conditions: At least 0.8 g combined EPA+DHA per serving of conventional food or dietary supplement.
The combined quantity per serving must be declared as described in the letter.
Dietary supplements bearing the claim must provide no more than 5 g/day combined EPA+DHA when used as labeled.
Qualifying evidence language, general labeling requirements and other letter nutrient factors apply.
source_locators: Letter section I.C safety, section IV.C minimum amount, conclusions

substances: cocoa flavanols in high-flavanol cocoa powder
annotations.regulatory_summary: This qualified claim concerns cardiovascular risk, and applies to high-flavanol cocoa powder or qualifying foods containing it.
use_conditions: Powder must contain at least 4% naturally conserved cocoa flavanols and at least 200 mg flavanols per RACC.
Foods containing the powder require at least one cocoa-powder RACC as an ingredient per food RACC, plus other letter conditions.
Eligible foods must meet low-fat, low-saturated-fat and low-cholesterol definitions and applicable other factors.
Regular cocoa powder and chocolate are outside this claim; qualifying language is required.

annotations.regulatory_summary: Qualifying low-sodium foods may bear conditional hypertension risk-reduction labeling.
use_conditions: All applicable 21 CFR 101.14 requirements apply, and the food must meet 21 CFR 101.61 low-sodium nutrient criteria.
Wording must express possible risk reduction, name sodium and high blood pressure, and acknowledge multiple risk factors.
The label may not quantify a degree of risk reduction; additional physician wording applies if pressure thresholds are defined.
